OD-B10-S01-T01.line: A month you have sat at my table, man of Troy, and still I hunger for the tale. Tell it again — the horse, the ships, the burning.
OD-B10-S01-T01.direction: hosts and listens, cup in hand

OD-B10-S01-T02.line: Take this bag of oxhide, Odysseus — every rough wind is bound inside, sewn shut with silver wire. I loose the West Wind only; let it carry you home to Ithaca.

OD-B10-S01-T03.line: Nine days and nights he held the sheet unsleeping, till the watch-fires of Ithaca winked on the shore. Then sleep took him at the helm.
OD-B10-S01-T03.direction: marks the turning of the voyage

OD-B10-S01-T04.line: His men eyed the bag and muttered of gold and silver. They cut the silver wire — and the winds burst shrieking out, and hurled them wailing back to Aeolia.

OD-B10-S01-T05.line: Out of my island — out, worst of living men! You come back cursed; the blessed gods themselves hate you. I give no help to what heaven hunts.

OD-B10-S02-T01.line: They came to the Laestrygonian land, where a narrow harbor lies ringed by sheer cliffs, and the fleet slid in as into a closed hand.
OD-B10-S02-T01.direction: sets the trap of the harbor

OD-B10-S02-T02.line: Not I. I make fast to the rock outside.
OD-B10-S02-T02.direction: moors alone beyond the cliff mouth

OD-B10-S02-T03.line: Three men went inland to learn who ate bread in that country. At the spring a girl tall as a tower met them, and pointed the way to her father's house.

OD-B10-S02-T04.line: Gods — the king snatched up my man and made his supper of him.

OD-B10-S02-T05.line: Then the Laestrygonians came in thousands, giants and not men. From the cliffs they speared the crews like fish, and rained down boulders till the trapped ships splintered.

OD-B10-S02-T06.line: Cut the cable! Bend to the oars, all of you, or we die with them!

OD-B10-S03-T01.line: One ship alone reached Aeaea, Circe's island. Two days and two nights they lay on the shore, eating their hearts with grief and weariness.

OD-B10-S03-T02.line: Smoke rises inland — some hearth burns beyond the oaks. But first, meat: this stag will feed us all tonight.

OD-B10-S03-T03.line: Two companies, friends. Eurylochus leads one and I the other — now shake the lots in the helmet.

OD-B10-S03-T04.line: The lot falls to me. Come then, you twenty-two — and gods keep the rest of you by the ship.

OD-B10-S04-T01.line: Weave and shine, weave and shine — so runs the thread, so runs the world.
OD-B10-S04-T01.direction: sings at the loom, beasts fawning

OD-B10-S04-T02.line: Go in if you must. I smell a snare in all this sweetness — I stay outside.
OD-B10-S04-T02.direction: hangs back at the shining doors

OD-B10-S04-T03.line: Drink deep, strangers — cheese and barley, pale honey, Pramnian wine. Now the wand: go to the sty where you belong.
OD-B10-S04-T03.direction: serves the cup, strikes each man

OD-B10-S04-T04.line: They took on the bristles and snouts and bodies of swine — but their minds stayed human, and they wept, remembering.

OD-B10-S04-T05.line: In with you. Acorns and cornel-berries — the proper food of what you are now.

OD-B10-S04-T06.line: They are gone, Odysseus — all of them! They went in at the shining doors and not one came out. I waited long, and called, and no man answered.

OD-B10-S05-T01.line: Bind on my sword and say no more, Eurylochus. Necessity drives — I go alone.
OD-B10-S05-T01.direction: slings sword and bow, strides inland

OD-B10-S05-T02.line: Where now, unlucky man, alone through these hills and knowing nothing of the ground? Your friends are penned as pigs in Circe's sties — and you march straight in to join them.

OD-B10-S05-T03.line: Here — take this herb of power and carry it against her drugs. The gods call it moly: black at the root, its flower white as milk. Hard for mortal men to dig, but the gods can do all things.
OD-B10-S05-T03.direction: pulls the herb from the earth

OD-B10-S05-T04.line: When she strikes you with her wand, draw your sword and rush her as if to kill. And before you go to her bed, make her swear the great oath of the gods that she plots no further harm — lest she strip you naked and unman you.
OD-B10-S05-T04.direction: lays out each step, then vanishes

OD-B10-S06-T01.line: Drink it all, stranger. Now — to the sty, and lie down with your friends!

OD-B10-S06-T02.line: But the herb held. The drug rolled off him like water off oiled wood, and he stood before her unchanged.
OD-B10-S06-T02.direction: the moly does its silent work

OD-B10-S06-T03.direction: shrinks back as he rushes sword-first

OD-B10-S06-T04.line: You are Odysseus — the man of many turns that Hermes always said would come from Troy. Sheathe your sword; come to my bed instead, that we may learn to trust each other.

OD-B10-S06-T05.line: First swear the great oath, goddess: no new harm against me, nothing planned while I lie unarmed in your house.

OD-B10-S06-T06.line: She swore, and her women bathed and dressed him and set the feast — but he sat with untouched hands. What honest man eats while his friends stand penned as swine?

OD-B10-S07-T01.line: Come, I will show you. This salve undoes what the other wrought.

OD-B10-S07-T02.line: The bristles fell away, and they stood up men again — younger than before, taller, and fairer to look upon.

OD-B10-S07-T03.direction: opens the pens, stands aside from the weeping reunion

OD-B10-S07-T04.line: Even my heart, which does not melt, is moved. Go down, beach your ship and bring the rest of your men — my halls will hold you all.

OD-B10-S07-T05.line: Haul the ship high and follow me — your shipmates sit feasting alive in Circe's hall. Eurylochus cries snare and ruin; I say the danger is past, and hanging back now costs more than you fear.

OD-B10-S07-T06.line: Sit, eat your meat and drink your wine, day upon day, till the heart comes back into your chests.
OD-B10-S07-T06.direction: presides over the long year of feasting

OD-B10-S08-T01.line: Circe, keep now the promise that you made me: send me home. My own heart strains for Ithaca, and my men's hearts with mine — will you loose us at last?

OD-B10-S08-T02.line: To the house of Death? Before Ithaca I must sail down to Hades and question blind Tiresias of Thebes? Then that is the road, though it breaks every heart aboard.

OD-B10-S08-T03.line: Set your mast and sit still — the North Wind will carry you across Ocean to Persephone's grove of poplar and willow. There dig a trench a cubit square, and pour to all the dead honey and milk, sweet wine, water, and white barley. Bleed a ram and a black ewe into it — the dead will come, but hold them from the blood until Tiresias has drunk.
OD-B10-S08-T03.direction: maps the road to the dead

OD-B10-S08-T04.direction: wakes on the roof, missteps, falls, neck breaks

OD-B10-S08-T05.line: They put out grieving for a road no living ship should sail — and behind the dark prow Circe sent a fair following wind, a good companion.

OD-B11-S01-T01.line: The ship came to deep-flowing Ocean's edge, to the land of the Cimmerians, wrapped in mist and cloud, where the shining sun never looks down.

OD-B11-S01-T02.line: By milk and honey, wine and white barley, I call you, nations of the dead — but stand off from the blood!
OD-B11-S01-T02.direction: digs the trench, cuts the victims' throats, bares his sword

OD-B11-S01-T03.line: Then they came — brides and unwed boys, old men worn with toil, girls with grief still fresh, warriors in their bloodied armor — crowding round the trench with a cry that made the cheeks go pale.

OD-B11-S01-T04.line: Back — back, all of you! None drinks before Tiresias of Thebes.
OD-B11-S01-T04.direction: holds the blade over the trench

OD-B11-S02-T01.direction: drifts forward first, unburied, before all the dead

OD-B11-S02-T02.line: No enemy killed him — wine, and the god's own drowsiness. He slept on Circe's roof, forgot the long ladder, fell, and broke his neck; and now he begs for fire and burial on Aeaea.

OD-B11-S02-T03.line: Burn me with all my armor and heap a mound by the grey sea, for an unlucky man that men to come may know of. And plant above it the oar I pulled while I lived among my friends — will you do this for me?

OD-B11-S02-T04.line: All this I will do, poor Elpenor — I will leave nothing undone. When I stand again on Aeaea, fire and mound and oar shall be yours.

OD-B11-S03-T01.line: The blood is dark and sweet. Now I know you, son of Laertes.
OD-B11-S03-T01.direction: stoops, drinks, lifts the golden staff

OD-B11-S03-T02.line: You seek a honey-sweet homecoming, but a god will make it bitter. The Earthshaker holds his grudge — you blinded the son he loved, and he does not forget.

OD-B11-S03-T03.line: Hear me, all of you: when you come to Thrinacia, where the cattle of the Sun graze, keep your hands from those herds. Harm them, and I foretell ruin for ship and crew — and if you yourself escape, you come home late and wretched, on a stranger's ship, with every companion lost.
OD-B11-S03-T03.direction: raises his voice to the whole crew

OD-B11-S03-T04.line: Blood in your own hall, an oar on your shoulder, a long walk inland till the sea itself is forgotten.
OD-B11-S03-T04.direction: foretells return, slaughter of suitors, the inland oar journey

OD-B11-S03-T05.line: And there, far from salt water, he must plant the oar and sacrifice to Poseidon; then death will come to him off the sea, gentle as mist, in a sleek old age with his people blessed around him.

OD-B11-S04-T01.line: Come, mother — drink of the blood and know me. It is I, alive, your son.
OD-B11-S04-T01.direction: lowers the sword from the trench

OD-B11-S04-T02.line: And Penelope — my wife, my son, my old father — tell me everything.
OD-B11-S04-T02.direction: listens hungrily to news of home

OD-B11-S04-T03.line: No sickness took you, then. It was longing — longing for me, for my counsels and my gentleness — that stole the honey of your life. My going killed you, mother.
OD-B11-S04-T03.direction: receives the truth like a wound

OD-B11-S04-T04.line: Mother — stay — let me hold you once!
OD-B11-S04-T04.direction: clutches three times at empty shade

OD-B11-S05-T01.line: One at a time, and each shall drink, and each shall speak her line.
OD-B11-S05-T01.direction: orders the shades at sword point

OD-B11-S05-T02.line: First came Tyro, nobly born, who loved the river Enipeus — and Poseidon took the river's shape, and of that bed came Pelias and Neleus. Speak, Tyro; the blood is yours.
OD-B11-S05-T02.direction: grants the first shade her turn

OD-B11-S05-T03.line: Then came Antiope and Alcmene, Megara and sorrowing Epicaste, Chloris, Leda, Iphimedeia, Phaedra, Ariadne — Maera, Clymene, and hateful Eriphyle, each with her story at her lips.
OD-B11-S05-T03.direction: calls the roll of famous women

OD-B11-S05-T04.line: And the trench became a living book of mothers: desire and birth, crime and death, line after line of the world's begetting.

OD-B11-S06-T01.line: Then the shade of Agamemnon, lord of men, drank and knew him and wept — crying that no sea took him, but Aegisthus and his own accursed wife, who cut him down at his own feast as a man fells an ox at the manger.
OD-B11-S06-T01.direction: gives the king's shade the blood

OD-B11-S06-T02.line: He heard Cassandra's dying cry above him as he lay. And the wife turned away — she would not even draw down his eyelids as he went to the house of Death.

OD-B11-S06-T03.line: So take his warning, Odysseus: put in to your own land secretly, not openly. Show your full mind to no woman, not even a faithful wife — the day of trusting them is done.

OD-B11-S06-T04.line: And one thing the king begged to know: does Orestes live — in Orchomenus, in sandy Pylos, with Menelaus in wide Sparta? But Odysseus could tell him nothing, and there was no comfort in the dark.

OD-B11-S07-T01.line: Then came the shade of Achilles, son of Peleus, and with him Patroclus and brave Antilochus — and Ajax, standing apart.

OD-B11-S07-T02.line: Achilles, no man was ever more blessed, nor will be: alive we honored you like a god, and here you rule with power among the dead. Do not grieve at dying — you of all men.
OD-B11-S07-T02.direction: offers consolation the shade will scorn

OD-B11-S07-T03.line: Would you hear of Peleus, and of your son Neoptolemus? Of your father I know nothing — but of the boy I can speak truly, for I myself brought him from Scyros to the war.

OD-B11-S07-T04.line: In council he spoke first and best; in battle he never lagged in the crowd, but charged far ahead. When we crouched inside the wooden horse the other chiefs wept and trembled — he only gripped his sword-hilt and begged me to let him leap out. And he took his prize and sailed home unwounded.

OD-B11-S07-T05.line: At that the shade of swift-footed Achilles strode away in long steps across the asphodel meadow, rejoicing that his son was great.

OD-B11-S07-T06.line: Only Ajax, son of Telamon, stood apart, angry still over the arms of Achilles that Odysseus won. Soft words were called to him — but the shade answered nothing, and went away in silence among the dead.

OD-B11-S08-T01.line: Minos with the golden scepter, judging the dead — and huge Orion, herding before him the ghosts of the beasts he killed on lonely hills.
OD-B11-S08-T01.direction: stares across the meadow of the dead

OD-B11-S08-T02.line: Tityus stretched under the tearing vultures, Tantalus thirsting with water at his chin, Sisyphus shouldering his pitiless stone.

OD-B11-S08-T03.line: I am only shadow — the man himself feasts among the deathless gods and holds fair-ankled Hebe. But you, poor wretch — do you too haul some such doom as I hauled beneath the sun? Son of Zeus I was, and still I slaved for a lesser man, who sent me down even here to drag away the hound.
OD-B11-S08-T03.direction: looms with bow drawn among shrieking dead

OD-B11-S08-T04.line: But the dead came crowding in their tens of thousands with an unearthly cry, and green fear took him — that dread Persephone might send up the Gorgon's head from Hades.

OD-B11-S08-T05.direction: withdraws into the dark as the living man flees to his ship

OD-B12-S01-T01.line: The ship left Ocean's stream and came again to Aeaea, where young Dawn keeps her dancing-lawns; they beached her on the sand and slept where the surf broke.

OD-B12-S01-T02.line: At dawn they fetched Elpenor's body from Circe's roof, and wept, and burned him with all his armor, and heaped a mound above the ashes.

OD-B12-S01-T03.line: And on the crown of the mound they planted his shapely oar, as the dead man had asked.
OD-B12-S01-T03.direction: sets the oar in the earth

OD-B12-S01-T04.line: Unflinching men — you have gone down living to the house of Death; twice-dying, when all others die once. Eat now, and drink till nightfall; at dawn you sail, and I myself will show you the road.
OD-B12-S01-T04.direction: arrives with bread, meat, and red wine

OD-B12-S02-T01.line: Listen well, for the road ahead has teeth. First the Sirens, who enchant every man that comes near them; then a strait between two terrors, Scylla and Charybdis; and beyond, Thrinacia, where the Sun keeps his cattle.
OD-B12-S02-T01.direction: draws him aside from the crew

OD-B12-S02-T02.line: Knead sweet wax and stop your men's ears; if you yourself must hear, let them bind you upright to the mast — and bind you tighter when you beg. Hug Scylla's cliff and row for your lives, for better six men lost than the whole ship swallowed by Charybdis. And on Thrinacia touch nothing — leave the Sun's herds unharmed, and you may yet come home.

OD-B12-S02-T03.line: But tell me truly, goddess — when she strikes at my men, can I not stand to her with spear and sword and beat her off?

OD-B12-S02-T04.line: Stubborn man — still spoiling for war and toil, still refusing to bow even to the gods! She is not mortal; she is deathless evil, terrible and wild, and not to be fought. Against Scylla there is no defense but flight.

OD-B12-S02-T05.line: At dawn they went down to the swift ship, and the goddess sent a fair wind astern, filling the sail.

OD-B12-S03-T01.line: Then the wind fell to a dead calm — some god lulled the waves to sleep — and ahead lay the island of the Sirens.

OD-B12-S03-T02.line: Ears to me, each man in turn — this wax stays till we are long past that shore.
OD-B12-S03-T02.direction: kneads warm wax, seals every ear

OD-B12-S03-T03.line: They bound him hand and foot, upright in the mast-step, and beat the sea white beneath their oars past the flowering shore.

OD-B12-S03-T04.line: Come here, far-famed Odysseus, great glory of the Achaeans — stay your ship and hear our voices. No man has ever rowed past us till he heard the honeyed song from our lips, and went away delighted, knowing more than he knew. For we know all that Argives and Trojans suffered on Troy's wide plain by the will of the gods — we know everything that comes to pass on the nourishing earth.
OD-B12-S03-T04.direction: sing motionless from the flowered shore

OD-B12-S03-T05.line: Loose me! Loose me — I must hear it all!
OD-B12-S03-T05.direction: strains at the ropes, jerks his brows in signal

OD-B12-S03-T06.line: But Perimedes and Eurylochus rose and lashed him tighter still, and the crew rowed until the song sank beneath the sound of the sea.

OD-B12-S04-T01.line: Straightway smoke, and a great breaker, and the boom of surf: Charybdis, sucking down the salt water and spewing it high like a cauldron on fierce fire — and the oars flew from their frightened hands.

OD-B12-S04-T02.line: Row, friends — we have been in worse and lived, and this too we shall remember. Helmsman, hold her off that smoke and hug the cliff — keep to the rock, or you kill us all.
OD-B12-S04-T02.direction: hides the six-fold price to come

OD-B12-S04-T03.line: Come then, if you dare come at me.
OD-B12-S04-T03.direction: arms fully, scans the mist-hung rock face

OD-B12-S04-T04.direction: hoisted screaming from the benches into the cliff's mouth

OD-B12-S04-T05.line: Like a fisherman swinging his catch to shore she swung them up to her rock, screaming, and ate them at her door — still stretching out their hands to him. Of all he saw upon the sea, that was the most pitiful.

OD-B12-S05-T01.line: Free of the rocks, they raised the noble island of the Sun, and heard the lowing of cattle in the pens and the bleating of sheep — the herds of Helios, who sees all things.

OD-B12-S05-T02.line: Row on — we do not land here. Tiresias and Circe both warned me alike: our worst harm waits on that island. Call me merciless if you will, Eurylochus — I would keep you alive.

OD-B12-S05-T03.line: But Eurylochus had the weary crew behind him, and Odysseus yielded to one night's landing — first swearing every man by solemn oath to touch neither cow nor sheep, but eat only the stores that Circe gave.
OD-B12-S05-T03.direction: seals the compromise with an oath

OD-B12-S05-T04.line: Then a month of South Wind, blowing without end; and when the ship's stores gave out they scoured the island with bent hooks for fish and birds, hunger gnawing their bellies.

OD-B12-S05-T05.line: Remember what you swore, friends — those herds belong to the Sun. Fish, fowl, roots, anything — but not the cattle.
OD-B12-S05-T05.direction: walks the camp, holding the line

OD-B12-S06-T01.line: When the last of Circe's stores was gone, Odysseus went up-island to pray the gods for a road home — and they poured sweet sleep over his eyelids.
OD-B12-S06-T01.direction: separates the captain from his crew

OD-B12-S06-T02.line: All deaths are hateful, brothers, but hunger is the meanest death of all. Drive off the best of the Sun's cattle — better one gulp of the wave than wasting thin on a desert island. And we will build Helios a rich temple in Ithaca, and heap it with offerings.

OD-B12-S06-T03.line: No barley — strip young oak leaves. No wine — pour water. Now pray, and cut.
OD-B12-S06-T03.direction: leads the makeshift sacrifice, kills and roasts

OD-B12-S06-T04.line: Then the gods showed them portents: the flayed hides crawled, and the meat lowed on the spits, raw and roasted, with the voice of cattle.

OD-B12-S06-T05.line: Swift Lampetie of the trailing robes ran to Helios with the news, and the Sun cried out to Zeus: punish them, father, or I go down to Hades and shine among the dead.

OD-B12-S07-T01.line: What have you done — you have slaughtered the Sun's own herds while I slept! O father Zeus, you lulled me to my ruin. This is doom, and no offering on earth will unmake it.
OD-B12-S07-T01.direction: groans at the smell of roasting meat

OD-B12-S07-T02.line: Six days they feasted on the finest of the cattle; on the seventh the storm-wind fell, and they stepped the mast and stood out to open sea.

OD-B12-S07-T03.line: Now pay the Sun his price.
OD-B12-S07-T03.direction: piles a black cloud, strikes the mast with the bolt

OD-B12-S07-T04.line: The bolt burst the ship end to end; she spun, filled with sulphur-smoke, and the men went overboard like sea-crows around the black hull — and the god took their homecoming away.
OD-B12-S07-T04.direction: drowns the last of the crew

OD-B12-S07-T05.line: Hold together — keel and mast and I.
OD-B12-S07-T05.direction: lashes the wreckage with the ox-hide backstay

OD-B12-S07-T06.line: The wind drove him back to Charybdis; he clung to the wild fig tree like a bat till his timbers rose again from the whirl, then dropped and rowed with his hands. Nine days he drifted, and on the tenth night the gods brought him alone to Ogygia — to Calypso.
OD-B12-S07-T06.direction: carries the lone survivor to Calypso
